column2: GROUND CHANGE - rebuild the mechanism, not the tuning. The founder has rejected the current behaviour twice: 'the scroll fades still aren't what I want... when I scroll we still see a straight (now faded) but clear line where the black and white pages start.' OPEN design-refs/Claryo-Ground-Black.png AND design-refs/Claryo-Ground-White.png FIRST. They are the SAME CONTENT at two moments - identical heading, identical three cards. In one the whole page is black with white type; in the other the whole page is white with black type. The content did not move: THE GROUND UNDER THE ENTIRE PAGE CHANGED AND THE FOREGROUND INVERTED WITH IT. Founder's words for the behaviour: 'the whole page is black, until a certain point in the scroll where we pass over into the new section then the whole page fades into being white.' THE ARCHITECTURE IS THE PROBLEM. Today each section owns a ground via data-register and a SectionSeam transitions between them, so a boundary is ALWAYS somewhere on screen and softening it only turned a hard line into a faded one. Replace that with a single page-level ground: exactly ONE ground exists at any moment, it covers the whole viewport, and crossing a threshold cross-fades the entire ground while the foreground tokens invert in step. If a boundary between two grounds can ever appear on screen, the candidate has not built this. CONSTRAINTS. The register vocabulary stays - canvas/product/technical still decide WHICH ground is current - but a register change must apply page-wide rather than per-section. The hero demos are §3 protected and must not be dimmed or slowed by the ground change. The ambient field and venue wireframe are founder-approved and live in the product register; they must survive. Every existing floor stays green: tests/reveal.spec.ts requires a reveal to end fully readable, tests/themes.spec.ts requires AA on every register and a visible shape on every filled control, and the reduced-motion floor requires the page to be static and complete with prefers-reduced-motion - the ground must settle to one resolved state there, never mid-fade. All four palettes must still work. Take a genuinely different MECHANISM from the other candidates - a fixed backdrop layer that cross-fades, a scroll-driven token swap on the root, a full-viewport blend layer, and a stacked pair of grounds cross-faded by scroll progress are all different starting points.
